accuracy.evidence: The order taught (have a go, try another way, look for a clue, ask a friend, ask a grown-up) matches the 'brain, book, buddy, boss' routine common in UK infant classrooms and Newman's account of adaptive help seeking: ask after effort, ask for the help you need (a hint or explanation), not for the answer. The safety exception (hurt, unsafe, unwell, someone unkind: tell a grown-up at once) matches standard safeguarding advice for young children and is never framed as 'try first'. The adult note separates instrumental and executive help-seeking without overclaiming effect sizes.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the real slips at five and six: asking before trying (the grown-up rung tapped first gives 'What have you tried?'; challenge 'first'; m8), sitting stuck or repeating the same try (the stuck meter rises and Pip's face turns cross; m2, m7; challenge 'when'), thinking asking is babyish (challenge 'brave', m1), vague asks like 'I can't do it' (the bubble rejects them with a reason; challenge 'best', m6), asking for the answer rather than a clue (challenge 'clue', m3, the visual sorter), and wrongly 'trying first' when hurt (sort step, challenge 'now', p4, m4).

lab_distinct.evidence: No other lab models a help ladder: the learner moves a character up four ordered rungs, the lab refuses skipped rungs and repeats, and a five-segment stuck meter and changing face show the cost of sitting stuck. Step 3 builds a three-slot speech bubble from good and bad word cards, and step 4 is a safety sort of six problems. The 30% shingle gate passed against every other flagship lab, including the emotions lab flagfeel.

lab_teaches.evidence: The rule is felt, not just read: in step 1 the word wall clue solves 'they' on rung two, so the learner sees that trying first often works; in step 2 the paint pot will not open until rung four, while the stuck meter climbs, so asking after effort is clearly the right move. Building the ask shows the three parts of a useful request, and the bad cards each explain why they fail. The free step cycles new problems (shoes on the wrong feet, a jigsaw, a reading book) where the right rung differs, so the learner has to judge rather than always climb to the top.

predictions.evidence: Each of the four guided steps opens with a locked prediction that has a tempting wrong option: ask the teacher straight away, keep trying the same way, the one-word 'Help!', and 'always try first' for a cut finger. The task then tests the prediction directly, so a wrong guess is corrected by what happens on the ladder, in the bubble or in the sort, not by a lecture.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven rotating challenge kinds (first, when, now, best, brave, clue, busy) with answer order rotated each round. Every wrong option has its own message that names the mistake and the fix, for example copying ('Copying skips the learning'), shouting at a busy teacher, waiting till home time when hurt, or thinking a clue is mean. Pip's face reflects the situation, and a run of correct answers counts stars.

readability.evidence: Kid text scores about FK -0.4 using short words and sentences ('Everyone gets stuck. Grown-ups get stuck too.'). Lab labels are one short line with numbered rungs. Adult text is about FK 6.7 and gives a concrete home routine: ask what they tried, give the smallest clue, praise the ask.

no_filler.evidence: Every paragraph carries one idea: the ladder order, the safety exception, the named mistakes, and the home routine. The family tip is a single action a parent can take tonight. The lab has no decorative steps; each step adds one new part of the skill (try first, ask after effort, ask clearly, know when not to wait).

mobile.evidence: Checked at iPhone 13 width (390 px): ladder rungs are big tap targets drawn on the canvas, with matching full-width buttons below, the bubble chips wrap in two columns, and sort cards can be dragged or sent with two large buttons. No text overlaps; the young class enlarges controls. The walkthrough ran with touch on the phone profile without errors.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin (rungs, chips, sort bins, new problem), the canvas has an aria-label that is updated with the problem, stuck meter level and Pip's rung, feedback lands in a polite live region, and the challenge answers sit in a labelled group. axe ran clean in light and dark themes.
